discovery: The electron recollision model of strong-field light-matter interaction and its quantum theory of high-harmonic generation

nominees.name: Paul B. Corkum
nominees.affiliation: University of Ottawa and National Research Council Canada

nominees.name: Maciej Lewenstein
nominees.affiliation: ICFO - The Institute of Photonic Sciences, Barcelona

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics: strong-field and attosecond physics
motivation: In 1993 Corkum, and independently Schafer with Kulander and co-workers, showed that an electron tunnel-ionized by an intense laser field is driven back to its parent ion, where it can recombine and emit a high-energy photon. This three-step recollision picture explained the harmonic cutoff at Ip + 3.17Up. In 1994 Lewenstein and collaborators turned it into a quantitative quantum theory. Recollision is the conceptual basis of attosecond science. It underlies attosecond pulse generation, laser-induced electron diffraction, tomographic orbital imaging, nonsequential double ionization and high-harmonic spectroscopy of molecules and solids. The 2023 prize honoured the experimental generation of attosecond pulses, but not the physical mechanism that made them understandable and controllable. These predictive theoretical frameworks transformed how physicists think about electrons driven by intense light, and they remain essential tools for interpreting every ultrafast strong-field measurement.
